Scope and evolution
About this document: scope and normative language

Purpose

The FinKore CoreDoc is a financial principles and rules standard. It states foundation-level obligations for financial meaning and control that FinKore domain specifications must refine. It is intended for accounting, audit, control, compliance, and financial-systems review.

The FinKore Core release version identifies the shared language-neutral behavioral baseline. It is distinct from conformance manifest/vector-file format versions and from versions assigned by consumer-owned tools or implementations.

Scope

The CoreDoc governs financial meaning, evidence, control behaviour, and history. It does not prescribe software design, storage, interfaces, programming languages, or conformance mechanics.

FinKore Core 2.0 does not define posting, double-entry ledgers, accounting dates or closed periods, tax, exchange-rate sourcing, reconciliation, settlement, accruals, depreciation, revenue recognition, statutory retention periods, or segregation-of-duties policy. This CoreDoc establishes none of them.

Normative language

SHALL, SHALL NOT, MUST, and MUST NOT are mandatory. SHOULD is a recommendation that may be departed from with documented justification. MAY expresses permission.

Reading guide

The five principles below describe the financial obligations that the domain specifications refine. Start with the principle relevant to your question:

PrincipleQuestion it addresses
Monetary integrityHow do amounts retain their value and currency through calculation?
Controlled financial stateWhich changes are permitted, and what happens when a change is rejected?
Financial history and evolutionHow are original facts preserved when later actions change their effect?
Approval integrityWhat was approved, by whom, and does that approval still apply?
Identifiable and determinable financial meaningCan a reviewer identify the subject, distinguish conditions, and reproduce the outcome?

Each rule gives its obligation, explains why this matters, then describes its interpretation and boundaries. Relevant FinKore domains links to the precise specification clauses. The CORE-* identifiers provide stable references; the dates record each rule's normative evolution.

CORE-001 · 4 rules

Monetary Integrity

Monetary information must retain the amount, currency, precision, and allocation meaning needed to prevent a value from being silently changed or misapplied.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-12

CORE-001.1

Amount and currency are inseparable

Link to this rule #

Rule

A monetary value SHALL contain an exact base-10 amount and a currency. An amount SHALL NOT be interpreted as monetary value without its currency.

Why this matters

The same number has different financial meaning in different currencies. Treating currency as display-only can misstate a balance or transaction.

Interpretation

Currency identifies the monetary unit; it does not supply an exchange rate. Negative and zero amounts retain ordinary numeric meaning unless a consuming domain declares a business restriction.

Boundaries

This rule does not determine permitted currencies, private-currency treatment, or exchange-rate policy.

Relevant FinKore domains

Money representation — MONEY-REPRESENTATION-001 to -004; Currency — MONEY-CURRENCY-005.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-001.2

Exact calculation and explicit rounding

Link to this rule #

Rule

Where a monetary calculation has an exactly representable result, it SHALL preserve that result. Precision reduction SHALL use a declared rounding rule and SHALL NOT select a rounding method or target scale implicitly.

Why this matters

Undeclared rounding changes financial value without an accountable policy decision. Exact calculation identifies where rounding was intentionally applied.

Interpretation

A rounding rule identifies both target scale and mode. A currency's customary minor-unit scale is not, by itself, a rounding instruction.

Boundaries

This rule does not select a business's rounding, tax, or statutory convention.

Relevant FinKore domains

Money arithmetic — MONEY-ARITHMETIC-007 and -008; Money rounding — MONEY-ROUNDING-001 and -004 to -007; Rates — MONEY-RATE-005 and -006.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-001.3

Incompatible currencies are not combined or compared

Link to this rule #

Rule

Monetary amounts SHALL be added, subtracted, ordered, or treated as numerically equal only when their currencies are compatible. Conversion SHALL be explicit; incompatibility SHALL NOT be silently resolved.

Why this matters

Combining EUR and USD without a stated conversion basis produces a number with no reliable financial interpretation.

Interpretation

In the current Money specification, compatibility requires the same ISO 4217 currency identifier. A mismatch is a rejected domain outcome, not zero or equal.

Boundaries

FinKore Core 2.0 does not specify rate source, rate date, or foreign-exchange accounting.

Relevant FinKore domains

Currency — MONEY-CURRENCY-003 and -004; Money arithmetic — MONEY-ARITHMETIC-001 and -002; Comparison — MONEY-COMPARISON-001 to -004.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

CORE-001.4

Allocation conserves the source value

Link to this rule #

Rule

An allocation SHALL preserve the source currency and return results whose exact sum equals the source amount. It SHALL NOT drop, duplicate, create, or destroy allocation units.

Why this matters

An unexplained residual between a cost or payment and its assignments prevents reconciliation.

Interpretation

The allocation scale and method are declared inputs. The declared result order governs distribution of an indivisible remainder.

Boundaries

This rule does not determine which costs may be allocated or the commercial basis for an allocation ratio.

Relevant FinKore domains

Money allocation — MONEY-ALLOCATION-001 to -013.

CORE-002 · 4 rules

Controlled Financial State

A financial subject's current status and permitted changes must be determined by declared domain rules. A rejected action must not leave a partial outcome.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-002.1

Lifecycle changes require a declared valid transition

Link to this rule #

Rule

Where a financial subject has a lifecycle, it SHALL have one declared current state. Its state SHALL change only through a declared transition from that state after all applicable conditions have passed.

Why this matters

Lifecycle status can determine whether a financial action is permitted or final. An undeclared shortcut, including an assumed reverse transition, weakens control.

Interpretation

Each lifecycle declares its initial state, directed transitions, and terminal states. Labels such as “posted” or “final” do not independently establish effect.

Boundaries

This rule does not prescribe universal states or which events require a lifecycle.

Relevant FinKore domains

Workflow states — WORKFLOW-STATES-002, -004, -007, and -009; Transitions — WORKFLOW-TRANSITION-001 to -005; Terminal states — WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-001 to -004; Entity lifecycle — ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001 to -006.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-001.4Allocation conserves the source valueNext rule · CORE-002.2 →Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutating

CORE-002.2

Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutating

Link to this rule #

Rule

A proposed financial change SHALL be evaluated against the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before it becomes observable. Validation or transition-condition evaluation SHALL NOT itself alter domain data.

Why this matters

Controls spanning several facts fail if each fact is assessed alone. State changed while checking a condition obscures the difference between attempt and success.

Interpretation

All applicable conditions must pass. For the same declared facts, a condition has the same result unless it identifies an external fact on which it depends.

Boundaries

This rule does not define a general authorization model or product-specific business validations.

Relevant FinKore domains

Workflow guards — WORKFLOW-GUARD-001 to -006; Entity validation — ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 to -003 and -006.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-002.1Lifecycle changes require a declared valid transitionNext rule · CORE-002.3 →Rejected actions have no partial financial effect

CORE-002.3

Rejected actions have no partial financial effect

Link to this rule #

Rule

A rejected financial action SHALL leave relevant observable financial state, financial data, and committed history unchanged, unless a governing rule expressly defines another failure effect.

Why this matters

A partly recognised failed change can create an unapproved balance, status, relationship, or audit trail that cannot be reconciled with the reported outcome.

Interpretation

This includes rejected transitions, entity mutations, audit appends and relationships, and evolution requests where the relevant specification defines non-mutation on failure.

Boundaries

This rule concerns domain-observable effects, not database transactions, retries, logs, or network-failure handling.

Relevant FinKore domains

Workflow transitions — WORKFLOW-TRANSITION-006 and -007; Entity mutability — ENTITY-MUTABILITY-004; Entity evolution — ENTITY-EVOLUTION-023 to -025; Audit errors — AUDIT-ERROR-001; Audit relationships — AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-012.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-002.2Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutatingNext rule · CORE-002.4 →Mutability is declared by state and field

CORE-002.4

Mutability is declared by state and field

Link to this rule #

Rule

For a subject with state-dependent mutability, the governing domain SHALL declare which fields may change in each state. A change targeting an immutable field SHALL be rejected.

Why this matters

“Final” status alone is too vague to determine what can still change. Unrestricted change to protected facts can detach a record from approval and history evidence.

Interpretation

Financial fields and operational metadata may have different rules, but a permitted exception must be expressly identified and meet audit requirements.

Boundaries

This rule does not make every field immutable after approval, posting, or a terminal state, and does not select a domain's field policy.

Relevant FinKore domains

Entity mutability — ENTITY-MUTABILITY-001 to -007.

CORE-003 · 4 rules

Financial History and Evolution

Material financial history must be attributable, reconstructible, and resistant to destructive rewriting. A later action may alter current effect but not conceal the earlier financial fact.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-003.1

A committed event preserves essential evidence

Link to this rule #

Rule

A committed financial event SHALL preserve a stable event identity, declared event type, affected financial subject, and unambiguous occurrence time. It SHALL identify the responsible actor when known.

Why this matters

Without these facts, a reviewer cannot determine what occurred, what it affected, when it took effect, or who was accountable.

Interpretation

Event type is declared domain meaning, not an inference from a technical action or label. An unknown or absent actor shall not be represented as an invented one.

Boundaries

This rule does not require an event for every operational occurrence or a universal event-type catalogue.

Relevant FinKore domains

Audit events — AUDIT-EVENT-001 to -008; Audit actors — AUDIT-ACTOR-001 to -004.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-002.4Mutability is declared by state and fieldNext rule · CORE-003.2 →Committed history is not destructively rewritten

CORE-003.2

Committed history is not destructively rewritten

Link to this rule #

Rule

A committed financial-history event and an explicitly recorded ordering relationship SHALL NOT be replaced, modified, removed, or silently reordered.

Why this matters

History cannot support reconstruction, investigation, or accountability if past events can disappear or change without trace.

Interpretation

Resubmitting an existing event identity is rejected rather than creating another committed instance. Arbitrary storage or retrieval order is not evidence of financial sequence when order was not explicitly recorded.

Boundaries

This rule does not impose event sourcing, global distributed order, or indefinite record retention.

Relevant FinKore domains

Audit append-only history — AUDIT-APPEND-001 to -004 and -006; Audit relationships — AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-009 and -014.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-003.3

Corrections and related evolution preserve original facts

Link to this rule #

Rule

A correction, reversal, void, or supersession SHALL preserve a verifiable relationship to the affected original subject or event. It SHALL NOT erase or rewrite original financial facts or history, and these concepts SHALL NOT be silently treated as interchangeable.

Why this matters

These actions can have different financial effects. A reviewer must distinguish a correction from a reversal or void and reconstruct both original and later facts.

Interpretation

Eligibility and detailed consequences are declared by the composing domain or lifecycle policy, not inferred from state or display labels.

Boundaries

This rule does not define accounting entries, effective dates, or business eligibility for these actions.

Relevant FinKore domains

Entity evolution — ENTITY-EVOLUTION-004, -006, and -008 to -023; Audit relationships — AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-001 to -013.

Rule history

CORE-003.4

Redaction preserves evidence of history

Link to this rule #

Rule

Financial-history content MAY be redacted only under identified policy or authority. Redaction SHALL remain distinguishable from original absence and preserve the event identity, type, affected subject, occurrence time, actor attribution, and recorded relationships needed to evidence the event.

Why this matters

Confidentiality can be necessary, but deleting evidence of an event makes its history unreconstructible. A reviewer must know that a value was withheld.

Interpretation

Redaction of committed logical history produces an event evidencing that redaction. Access-time masking may supplement it but is not source-event mutation.

Boundaries

This rule does not establish privacy law, retention law, cryptographic deletion, or access-control policy.

Relevant FinKore domains

Audit redaction — AUDIT-REDACTION-001 to -007; Audit append-only history — AUDIT-APPEND-001 and -004; Audit actors — AUDIT-ACTOR-006.

Rule history

CORE-004 · 4 rules

Approval Integrity

An approval is a financial-control decision about a specified subject and facts. It is distinct from technical access to submit an action.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-004.1

Approval requirements state subject, eligibility, and outcome

Link to this rule #

Rule

An approval requirement SHALL identify the subject requiring approval, eligible decision-maker or eligibility rule, and the outcome that satisfies or rejects it. Eligibility SHALL be evaluated independently from technical ability to submit a request.

Why this matters

Technical permission is not evidence that appropriate business approval was given. Declared eligibility and outcome criteria make the control testable.

Interpretation

A requirement may be conditional, but retains stable identity in its approval context. A decision-maker must meet the requirement at evaluation time.

Boundaries

This rule does not establish authentication, role-based access control, maker-checker separation, delegated approval, or conflict-of-interest policy.

Relevant FinKore domains

Approval requirements — APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-001 to -007; Approval decisions — APPROVAL-DECISION-004 and -012.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-003.4Redaction preserves evidence of historyNext rule · CORE-004.2 →Missing facts do not create an approval exemption

CORE-004.2

Missing facts do not create an approval exemption

Link to this rule #

Rule

An approval condition SHALL be evaluated against identified domain facts. If a required fact is absent, the requirement SHALL fail or remain unresolved; it SHALL NOT be silently treated as not applicable.

Why this matters

Treating missing information as an exemption can bypass a control when its assessment information is unavailable.

Interpretation

For the same condition and facts, applicability is deterministic. Presentation state and unspecified authorization policy are not implicit approval inputs.

Boundaries

This rule does not determine which approval conditions a business must impose.

Relevant FinKore domains

Approval conditions — APPROVAL-CONDITION-001 to -006.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-004.1Approval requirements state subject, eligibility, and outcomeNext rule · CORE-004.3 →Decisions remain tied to their facts and history

CORE-004.3

Decisions remain tied to their facts and history

Link to this rule #

Rule

An approval decision SHALL identify its requirement, deciding actor, outcome, time, and relevant subject facts or state. It SHALL NOT be assumed valid after relevant facts change, and a committed decision SHALL NOT be overwritten or removed from logical approval history.

Why this matters

Approval is meaningful only in relation to what was approved. Preserving the decision and factual basis shows whether later change needs fresh consideration.

Interpretation

The application or a higher-level policy determines which changed facts are relevant or material. Portable decisions are approved and rejected. Current FinKore Approval validity rules define withdrawal, expiration, and supersession as lifecycle evidence that affects current effectiveness without rewriting the committed Decision.

Boundaries

This rule does not define materiality, delegation, quorum, or authorization policy.

Relevant FinKore domains

Approval decisions — APPROVAL-DECISION-001 to -008 and -012; Approval conditions — APPROVAL-CONDITION-003; Approval validity — APPROVAL-VALIDITY-001 to -016.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-004.2Missing facts do not create an approval exemptionNext rule · CORE-004.4 →Chain status follows declared requirements and decisions

CORE-004.4

Chain status follows declared requirements and decisions

Link to this rule #

Rule

An approval chain SHALL declare whether its applicable requirements are sequential or unordered. It SHALL be approved only when every applicable requirement is approved; it SHALL remain pending while an applicable requirement is pending unless an effective rejection determines the declared outcome.

Why this matters

A chain that appears complete before every required approval is effective permits a financial action without its intended control.

Interpretation

A sequential chain does not activate a later requirement before its predecessor is satisfied. An unordered chain is not silently treated as sequential.

Boundaries

This rule does not define a universal sequence, rejection policy, or quorum.

Relevant FinKore domains

Approval chains — APPROVAL-CHAIN-001 to -010; Approval requirements — APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-005.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-005 · 3 rules

Identifiable and Determinable Financial Meaning

Financial meaning must be attributable to stable subjects and declared facts. A reviewer must distinguish material conditions and reproduce results from stated context.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-005.1

Continuing financial subjects retain stable identity

Link to this rule #

Rule

A continuing financial subject SHALL have an identifier unique within its declared scope and stable throughout its lifecycle. Distinct subjects SHALL NOT share that identifier within the same scope.

Why this matters

Stable identity connects state, approvals, corrections, evidence, and accountability over time. A mutable or reusable display number cannot do so.

Interpretation

Identifiers are opaque: their format does not establish mutable financial facts. Import or migration preserves identity or records an explicit continuity mapping.

Boundaries

This rule does not require a global identifier format or universal identity scope.

Relevant FinKore domains

Entity identity — ENTITY-IDENTITY-001 to -006; Audit events — AUDIT-EVENT-004; Audit actors — AUDIT-ACTOR-001 to -003.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

← Previous rule · CORE-004.4Chain status follows declared requirements and decisionsNext rule · CORE-005.2 →Materially distinct conditions remain distinguishable

CORE-005.2

Materially distinct conditions remain distinguishable

Link to this rule #

Rule

Where the governing domain gives materially different meaning to absence, an explicit null, an unknown actor, a redacted value, a pending approval, a rejected approval, a not-applicable requirement, or zero monetary amount, those conditions SHALL remain distinguishable.

Why this matters

Collapsing these conditions can turn missing evidence into an exemption, hide a redaction, misattribute an action, or turn an absent value into zero.

Interpretation

The rule applies only to distinctions made material by the governing domain. It does not make every representational difference a financial distinction.

Boundaries

This rule does not require all domains to use the same representation or define every possible form of missing information.

Relevant FinKore domains

Audit changes — AUDIT-CHANGE-003; Audit actors — AUDIT-ACTOR-004; Audit redaction — AUDIT-REDACTION-002; Approval conditions — APPROVAL-CONDITION-002 and -006; Approval requirements — APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-005; Money representation — MONEY-REPRESENTATION-004.

Rule history

Introduced: Draft 0.4

Last updated: Draft 0.4

Last updated on: 2026-09-10

CORE-005.3

Evaluation follows declared facts and context

Link to this rule #

Rule

For the same declared inputs, financial state, and relevant context, a financial evaluation SHALL produce the same observable outcome. A dependency on an external fact SHALL be identified when it affects that outcome.

Why this matters

Reconciliation, challenge, and audit require reproducible outcomes from their stated basis. Hidden dependence prevents that review.

Interpretation

This covers rounding, allocation, approval conditions and chains, and workflow guards. It does not make external facts impermissible; it requires their relevance to be stated.

Boundaries

This rule does not define accounting dates, market-data sourcing, or a general snapshotting and retention regime for external facts.

Relevant FinKore domains

Money rounding — MONEY-ROUNDING-002; Money allocation — MONEY-ALLOCATION-012; Approval conditions — APPROVAL-CONDITION-005; Approval chains — APPROVAL-CHAIN-008; Workflow guards — WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 and -006; Audit append-only history — AUDIT-APPEND-006.

Relationship with specifications

CoreDoc
  -> Domain specifications
  -> Conformance artifacts
  -> Consumer implementations and verification

The CoreDoc supplies foundation-level financial obligations. Domain specifications define precise scope and behaviour; conformance artifacts make observable requirements concrete; consumer implementations realise and verify that behaviour. A lower layer may refine a CoreDoc rule but shall not silently contradict it.

When labels differ, /spec remains authoritative for precise domain behavior, and this CoreDoc remains authoritative for foundation-level rules and their normative evolution. /conformance publishes portable acceptance evidence for observable requirements; it is not a second specification. /agentic describes machine-understandable operation semantics and must reference, not replace, /spec. Consumer implementations and their execution results may provide additional evidence, but they are not sources of financial semantics.

Evolution of CoreDoc

Core Principle and Financial Rule identifiers are stable references. A CORE-XXX or CORE-XXX.N identifier SHALL NOT be reused for an unrelated principle or rule. A removed, replaced, or superseded rule remains traceable in historical records rather than being silently reassigned.

Introduced records entry into CoreDoc. Last updated and Last updated on record the most recent normative change. Editorial-only changes SHALL NOT update those fields.

Release summaries are maintained in FinKore Release Notes. They do not override CoreDoc or /spec.

Scope and deferred topics

This CoreDoc is limited to the current Money, Workflow, Audit, Approvals, and Financial Entities specifications. It makes no claim that unspecified future domains or policy choices have already been standardised.

Current deferred topics include private or non-fiat currency namespaces, minor-unit metadata policy, implementation resource limits, standardized Audit provenance fields, portable condition expressions, Workflow migration and distributed coordination, approval delegation and escalation, dynamic approver resolution, broader identity registries, concrete ledger or correction posting effects, post-finalization metadata policy, distributed Audit total ordering, and future ledger, reconciliation, payment, tax, and settlement domains.
